title: Pullback cube for the intrinsic semilinear alpha transformation
statement:
Let $C_1\leftarrow C_2\leftarrow\cdots$ be arbitrary commutative rings. On the small pro-etale sites of schemes use the strict semilinear operations of [def-sp-varying-ring-operations] and the open-unit-normalized $\beta$ and clopen-projection $\alpha$ of [def-sp-varying-ring-proper-open-arrows]. In this node write $P_v=D(v^*_{\bullet})$ for exact derived inverse image and $J_j=D(j_{!,\bullet})$ for open extension. Let $Q$ be $pk=ir$ with $k:U\hookrightarrow V$, $i:W\hookrightarrow Z$ quasi-compact open and $p:V\to Z$, $r:U\to W$ proper. Let $h:Z_1\to Z$, and base change all four vertices, writing $a:V_1\to V$, $c:W_1\to W$, $d:U_1\to U$ and $Q_1=(k_1,i_1,r_1,p_1)$ for the projections and induced square [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then the following two transformations from $P_{p_1}P_hJ_i$ to $J_{k_1}P_{r_1}P_c$ agree:
$$P_{p_1}P_hJ_i\xrightarrow{P_{p_1}\beta_{i,h}}P_{p_1}J_{i_1}P_c\xrightarrow{\alpha_{Q_1}P_c}J_{k_1}P_{r_1}P_c,$$
$$P_{p_1}P_hJ_i\cong P_aP_pJ_i\xrightarrow{P_a\alpha_Q}P_aJ_kP_r\xrightarrow{\beta_{k,a}P_r}J_{k_1}P_dP_r\cong J_{k_1}P_{r_1}P_c.$$
Use the specified pullback and open compositors. This is already an equality after exact localization of ordinary system transformations, before taking any proper direct-image mate.

source.place: Tag 0F7F (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-base-change), alpha-level open case; agent-written extension to arbitrary strict semilinear systems

proof.text: Put $T=V\times_ZW$, with projections $b:T\to V$, $q:T\to W$, and $s=(k,r):U\to T$. The geometric clause of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] says that $s$ is clopen, $bs=k$, and $qs=r$. The base changes $p_1,r_1$ remain proper, $i_1,k_1$ remain open and quasi-compact, by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] and [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change]. Thus the same geometric clause applies to $Q_1$. Write $T_1=V_1\times_{Z_1}W_1$, with $b_1,q_1,s_1$. Fibre-product uniqueness [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $T_1$ with $T\times_ZZ_1$. Its map $e:T_1\to T$ satisfies $be=ab_1$, $qe=cq_1$, $es_1=sd$, and identifies $s_1$ with the base change of $s$. In particular $T_1=s_1(U_1)\amalg T_1^c$ is a disjoint open cover. This uses no cartesianness of $Q$ itself.

source.place: Tag 0F7F (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-base-change), open case; clopen factorization of Tag 0F7B

proof.text: Work first in the ordinary abelian system categories of [def-sp-varying-ring-operations], not in their derived categories. Their identification as modules over the ring object on the sequence topos is supplied by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. In this paragraph stars and shrieks denote ordinary system functors. For $M\in\mathscr S_W$, put $F=p_1^*h^*i_!M$ and $G=k_{1!}r_1^*c^*M$. Let $L_M,R_M:F\to G$ be the two composites in the question before localization. The two cartesian open comparisons of [def-sp-varying-ring-proper-open-arrows] give an isomorphism $\rho_M:F\xrightarrow{\sim}b_{1!}A$, where $A=q_1^*c^*M$: first use $h^*i_!\cong i_{1!}c^*$ and then $p_1^*i_{1!}\cong b_{1!}q_1^*$. By the Hom bijection of [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], applied to the localized ringed sequence site, equality of $L_M,R_M$ is equivalent to equality of the adjuncts of $L_M\rho_M^{-1},R_M\rho_M^{-1}$. These adjuncts are $b_1^*L_M,b_1^*R_M$ preceded by the same map $A\to b_1^*F$. It therefore suffices to prove $b_1^*L_M=b_1^*R_M$.

source.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), Hom bijection on the ringed sequence site

proof.text: Record explicitly the ordinary normalization used in the restriction calculation. For any cartesian open square $(j,g,j',g_U)$, [def-sp-varying-ring-proper-open-arrows] defines $\beta_{j,g}^{-1}$ as the $j'_!\dashv j'^*$ transpose of $g_U^*u_j$ followed by the inverse-image compositor, where $u_j:1\to j^*j_!$ is the open unit. Consequently $j'^*\beta_{j,g}^{-1}\circ u_{j'}=g_U^*u_j$ under that compositor. Since both units are invertible, $j'^*\beta_{j,g}$ is the identity under the open-unit identifications. This is the adjunction triangle identity, with no single-level or derived evaluation argument. All the compositors here are the unit-preserving comparisons of [def-sp-varying-ring-operations].

For the clopen $s$, let $t:s_!\to s_*$ be the transpose of $u_s^{-1}$. By [def-sp-varying-ring-proper-open-arrows], $\pi_s=t^{-1}_{s^*(-)}\circ\eta_s$. The transpose equation and the $s^*\dashv s_*$ triangle identity give $s^*\pi_s=u_{s^*(-)}$; thus this is the identity under the open unit. Restrict the defining word $\alpha_Q=\beta_{i,p}$, then $b_!\pi_s q^*$, then the open and pullback compositors, along $k=bs$. The restriction of its first factor is the identity by step 3, that of its second factor is the identity just computed, and the final compositors identify $s^*q^*$ with $r^*$. Hence $k^*\alpha_Q$ is the canonical map $k^*p^*i_!\cong r^*i^*i_!\xrightarrow{r^*u_i^{-1}}r^*$. The identical computation with $s_1,b_1,q_1$ gives the corresponding formula for $k_1^*\alpha_{Q_1}$.

source.place: Tag 0F7F, alpha-level open case; ordinary clopen projection word of Tag 0F7B

proof.text: Now restrict both $L_M$ and $R_M$ along $k_1=b_1s_1$. Identify their common source with $r_1^*c^*i^*i_!M$ and their common target with $r_1^*c^*M$. For $L_M=(\alpha_{Q_1}c^*)\circ(p_1^*\beta_{i,h})$, step 3 makes the first comparison the identity after restriction through $k_1^*p_1^*\cong r_1^*i_1^*$; step 4 then gives $r_1^*c^*u_i^{-1}$. For $R_M$, restriction of $a^*\alpha_Q$ becomes $d^*k^*\alpha_Q=d^*r^*u_i^{-1}$ by step 4, and restriction of $\beta_{k,a}r^*$ is the identity by step 3. The equality $rd=cr_1$ identifies this with $r_1^*c^*u_i^{-1}$. Both source identifications use the same equality $hp_1k_1=icr_1=pkd$. The specified compositors [def-sp-varying-ring-operations] are the adjoints of identity-on-sections direct-image comparisons; the two rebracketings have the same such adjoint, so their identifications agree. This proves $s_1^*b_1^*L_M=s_1^*b_1^*R_M$, with the required compositors.

source.place: Tag 0F7F (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-base-change), selected-component computation; agent extension to strict semilinear systems

proof.text: On the complementary open $T_1^c$, the common target $b_1^*G\cong s_{1!}r_1^*c^*M$ restricts to zero. Indeed the clopen comparison $s_{1!}\cong s_{1*}$ is invertible by [def-sp-varying-ring-proper-open-arrows], and the direct-image section formula of [def-sp-varying-ring-operations] on an object $H\to T_1^c$ gives sections over $H\times_{T_1}U_1=\varnothing$, hence the zero module. Both restricted arrows are therefore zero. For each coefficient index and every pro-etale object $H\to T_1$, the two arrows agree after restriction to the covering $H\times_{T_1}U_1$ and $H\times_{T_1}T_1^c$. The uniqueness part of the sheaf axiom makes their values on each section equal [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Since ordinary system morphisms are compatible componentwise module maps [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], this proves equality of the ordinary system arrows $b_1^*L_M=b_1^*R_M$, and step 2 proves $L_M=R_M$. Their naturality in $M$ is inherited from the functorial words defining them, so the equality is one of system natural transformations.

source.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), disjoint-open section calculation; proetale.tex Tag 09AE (definition-extension-zero)

proof.text: Finally apply these ordinary natural transformations degreewise to arbitrary cochain complexes of systems. The exact additive inverse-image and open-extension functors of [def-sp-varying-ring-operations] preserve quasi-isomorphisms, and every map and compositor used above is the specified ordinary one localized in that definition and [def-sp-varying-ring-proper-open-arrows]. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], localization respects composition and carries the equality of the degreewise natural transformations to an equality of natural transformations on $D(\mathscr S_W)$. It is exactly the two displayed words in the statement, since $P_v=D(v^*_{\bullet})$ and $J_j=D(j_{!,\bullet})$. This proves the equality before any proper direct-image mate is taken and for arbitrary unbounded complexes; it does not infer equality from derived evaluations.
